parts.title: The Man Doom Hid Under His Castle
rows: Doom saved reality, then buried its past. Doom's Broken Worlds, part one.
As the last two universes collided, Doom's rival Reed Richards built a raft to get people out.
Doom took another route, gathering fragments from the worlds that had already been destroyed.
He stitched those fragments into one planet called Battleworld, where every survivor answered to him.
His subjects worshipped him as their god and knew nothing of the worlds they'd lost.
But some raft survivors remembered their old lives and started investigating the ruler who'd replaced their entire reality.
That search led beneath Doom's castle, to a hidden man. Why would a god need to hide him?

parts.title: The Hamburger That Earned Spider-Man a Favor
rows: The man beneath Doom's castle was keeping him a god. Doom's Broken Worlds, part two.
Miles Morales, one of the Spider-Men, had survived his universe's destruction. His mother had died before any of this.
While investigating Doom's power, Miles found the hidden Molecule Man beneath the castle, with an unexpectedly ordinary problem.
He was hungry. This was the same man supplying the cosmic power that kept Doom on his throne.
Miles reached into his pocket and handed him a hamburger, giving him something to eat.
The gesture earned Molecule Man's gratitude. Doom still had his throne, but Miles now had a favor coming.
A man who could help reshape reality now owed him. What could that favor actually give Miles back?

parts.title: Doom Lost His Power. Spider-Man Got His Favor.
rows: Doom's reign ended with an admission. Miles's favor was still waiting. Doom's Broken Worlds, part three.
Reed Richards, Doom's rival, confronted him over the world he'd built from everybody else's ruins.
Doom finally admitted Reed would have done a better job saving reality, despite everything Doom had managed to preserve.
Molecule Man agreed and took the power away from Doom, handing it to Reed instead.
Reed and his family helped rebuild the separate realities. Doom's patchwork planet would no longer be the only world.
Molecule Man also remembered the hamburger, and rewarded the kid who'd shared it with him.
Miles Morales got a home in the rebuilt reality. And his mother, who'd died before all this, was alive again.
That was Doom's Broken Worlds. Subscribe for more comic stories.
